article.Citation/Title: Rieser, N. M., Bitar, R., Halm, S., Rossgoderer, C., Gubser, L. P., Thevenaz, M., Kreis, Y., von Rotz, R., Nordt, C., Visentini, M., Moujaes, F., Engeli, E. J. E., Ort, A., Seifritz, E., Vollenweider, F. X., Herdener, M., & Preller, K. H. (2025). Psilocybin-assisted therapy for relapse prevention in alcohol use disorder: a phase 2 randomized clinical trial. eClinicalMedicine.
article.SD: 95% CI: psilocybin 14.31-19.29 days; placebo 10.97-16.63 days (abstinence-duration means paired with Cohen's d in Abstract)
article.InterventionDescription: Single 25 mg oral psilocybin capsule (vs mannitol placebo) in an 8-hour supervised outpatient dosing session, embedded in 5.5 hours of BRENDA-based psychotherapy (2 prep + 3 integration visits).

ae_events.Description: Non-serious adverse events after dosing: 13 in the psilocybin group, 7 in the placebo group; individual event types itemized only in Supplementary Table S11 (not provided).
Serious adverse events, all inpatient withdrawal treatments: 1 in the psilocybin group and 4 in the placebo group, per the study's (S)AE case report form.

article.Outcome: Co-primary endpoints were 'abstinence and mean alcohol use at 4-week follow-up' (Abstract/Methods), with no single explicit primary-of-the-two designation, so precedence rule (2) applies: the Abstract's Findings paragraph and the Results section both lead with the abstinence comparison before mean alcohol use. Abstinence duration itself was analyzed two ways in the text: (i) a Kaplan-Meier survival/Cox-regression analysis (Results: 'no significant difference in duration of abstinence (p = 0.55, ...) utilizing the Kaplan-Meier survival analysis'; Cox HR = 0.78, 95% CI 0.34-1.76, no p printed for the HR itself) and (ii) a group-mean comparison reported as 'duration of abstinence (p = 0.37, Cohen's d = 0.151)' later in the same Results paragraph (tied to the Fig. 2B boxplot). The Abstract states both together in one sentence ('p = 0.55, ... Cohen's d = 0.151'), pairing the KM p-value with the d-statistic from the separate group-mean test. This is an internal inconsistency in the article (the same d = 0.151 is paired with p = 0.55 in the Abstract but p = 0.37 in the Results narrative) that could not be resolved without inventing a decoding theory, so it is reported as printed and flagged here rather than silently reconciled. Outcome = 0.151 (Cohen's d for abstinence duration, psilocybin vs. placebo, 4-week follow-up) is taken verbatim from the Abstract/Results, chosen as the standardized effect size for the primary abstinence comparison per Tier-1 conversion priority (Cohen's d over an unconvertible HR).
article.SD: No t- or U-test statistic value is printed alongside Cohen's d = 0.151 anywhere in the text; only the 95% CIs for each group's mean abstinence duration are given in the same sentence as the d-statistic in the Abstract ('psilocybin mean = 16.80 days, 95% CI: 14.31-19.29; placebo mean = 13.80 days, 95% CI: 10.97-16.63'). These CIs are reported here as the paired dispersion measure. Fig. 2B's caption separately gives slightly different SDs (psilocybin SD = 10.71, placebo SD = 12.68) tied to slightly different means (16.61/13.79 vs. 16.80/13.80) for what appears to be the same analysis - a minor additional numeric inconsistency, noted but not used, since it is one step further removed from the Outcome value's own sentence.
article.PVal: 0.55 is used because it is the value printed in the same sentence as Cohen's d = 0.151 in the Abstract (the article's own headline pairing of this effect size). The Results section later re-uses the identical d = 0.151 with p = 0.37 instead (Mann-Whitney/t-test group comparison, Fig. 2B) - see the Outcome rationale for this unresolved internal inconsistency, which should go to human review.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: N = 37 is the 4-week-follow-up analysis population stated in the Abstract ('We included 37 participants who completed the 4-week follow-up ... psilocybin = 18, placebo = 19') and confirmed by Table 1 ('Sample size: Total 37, Psilocybin 18, Placebo 19') and the CONSORT flow diagram (Fig. 1: placebo arm reaches 19 at the 4-week/6th visit, psilocybon arm reaches 18). The Results-section sentence 'resulting in a final sample size of 37 participants (psilocybin: 19, placebo: 18)' reverses these two arm counts relative to the Abstract, Table 1, and Fig. 1 - an apparent typo in the source article. The majority-supported 18 psilocybin/19 placebo split (matching 3 of 4 places the numbers appear) was used; the discrepancy is flagged for human review rather than silently picked.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: All 14 elements are explicitly described: objective (Abstract/Introduction), design and setting (single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial at Psychiatric University Hospital Zurich), eligibility (age, DSM-5 AUD diagnosis, recent withdrawal treatment, detailed exclusion criteria), intervention/comparator (25 mg psilocybin vs. 100% mannitol placebo, identical capsules, BRENDA-based psychotherapy), outcomes (primary: abstinence and mean SU at 4-week follow-up; secondary endpoints listed), sample_size_power (G-Power 3.1 a priori calculation, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.95, n = 24/arm target, with underpowering from early termination discussed), randomization (stratified 1:1 by hospital pharmacy, stratification factors named), blinding (double-blind with identical capsules; blinding integrity explicitly assessed via allocation-guess question), statistical_methods (detailed Statistics section: Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, Mann-Whitney/t-tests, linear mixed models, Wilcoxon tests), results (fully reported with effect sizes and CIs throughout), harms (dedicated Safety assessment section and AE/SAE reporting), funding_coi (Funding and Declaration of interests sections with per-author detail).

article.PrimaryCare: Coded 0: the entire study (recruitment, dosing, psychotherapy, follow-up) was conducted through the Psychiatric University Hospital Zurich; the text does not mention any primary-care referral pathway, provider, or setting (contrast with trials that explicitly recruit via primary care).
article.Retention (%): Denominator = 40, the randomized sample (Fig. 1 CONSORT diagram: 21 randomized to placebo + 19 randomized to psilocybin, both arms fully proceeding to the dosing visit with no pre-dosing dropout). Numerator = 37, participants completing the 4-week primary endpoint (Abstract/Table 1). Retention = 37/40*100 = 92.5%. Note: the CONSORT flow-diagram text (Fig. 1) is OCR-garbled in the converted markdown (overlapping columns, stray symbols), so the 21/19 randomized split was cross-checked against the narrative dropout counts described in the same figure caption and is consistent with them.
article.AE_denominator: Coded 40 (all randomized/dosed participants: 19 psilocybin + 21 placebo per Fig. 1), since Safety assessment (vital signs, (S)AE case report forms) was applied 'at every visit' from the dosing visit onward across both arms, and the reported AE/SAE counts are explicitly broken out by arm (13/7 AEs, 1/4 SAEs) rather than restricted to completers only, supporting a full-randomized-sample denominator rather than the N=37 completer analysis population.
article.BaseStatus: Coded 'Severe' from Table 1's DSM-5 AUD severity breakdown for the full analyzed sample: 'AUD severity (mild:moderate:severe, DSM5) 3:6:28' - 28/37 (75.7%) severe, the modal and majority category.
article.PercentFem: Table 1 / Abstract: 'female:male = 14:23' of the N=37 analysis sample. 14/37*100 = 37.8%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Table 1, 'Race and ethnicity': Caucasian = 37, African = 1, with a footnote that 'the total exceeds 100% because one participant selected multiple categories' (i.e., the 1 African-identifying participant also selected Caucasian). Non-white/BIPOC = 1 of 37 = 2.7%.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Trial conducted at the Psychiatric University Hospital Zurich, Switzerland (Methods/Study design; ethics approvals from Swiss cantonal and federal bodies). Coded 'NonUS'.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0: participants were required to have completed withdrawal treatment within 6 weeks of enrollment and passed extensive exclusion criteria (other major psychiatric or substance use disorders, suicidal-behavior history, family history of schizophrenia/schizoaffective/bipolar disorder, unstable physical health, limited hallucinogen-use history). Discussion also notes the sample was 'most Caucasian, reflecting the population distribution in Switzerland,' with the authors themselves calling for 'more diverse populations' in future trials. This is a highly screened, help-seeking volunteer sample, not reflective of the broader real-world AUD population.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: No income, employment, insurance, or other SES-related inclusion criterion or description is reported anywhere in the text. Coded 0.
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1: randomization was stratified by age, sex, and AUD severity to balance these factors (Randomization and blinding); an exploratory subgroup analysis examined prior psychedelic experience as a moderator of outcome; a sensitivity analysis standardized alcohol-use outcomes by body weight/BMI.
article.Implementation Outcome: Coded 0: no feasibility, acceptability, fidelity, reach, adoption, or sustainability outcome is reported. The allocation-guess check assesses blinding integrity, not implementation/fidelity, and is not treated as an implementation outcome here.
article.MortalityMeasured: Coded 0: mortality is not named as a measured or reported outcome anywhere in the text, and no deaths are reported among the AE/SAE counts (the SAEs are explicitly described as inpatient withdrawal treatments only).

ae_events.Rieser 2025_AE01: Text gives only aggregate non-serious AE counts by arm ('we observed a total of 13 AEs in the psilocybin and 7 in the placebo group'), with a pointer to 'Safety outcomes are reported in Supplementary Table S11' for the itemized breakdown, which is not part of the converted text provided. No individual event types, per-event counts, severity grades, or onset timing are available in-text beyond the summary statement 'The psilocybin dose (25 mg) administered in our study was well-tolerated.' Defaulted to Mild per the rubric's under-specified-AE rule (no intervention-need or persistence signal), SeverityIndeterminate=Y, SeveritySource=rubric (no author grading visible in this text), and NAffected='.' since the 13/7 figures are event counts for an unspecified mix of types, not a single AE type's participant count.
ae_events.Rieser 2025_AE02: Text states explicitly: 'One serious adverse event occurred in the psilocybin and four in the placebo group, all related to inpatient withdrawal treatments' (Abstract), and 'Additionally, 1 SAE in the psilocybin and 4 in the placebo group occurred, all of which were inpatient withdrawal treatments' (Results). Graded Severe because inpatient hospitalization is an explicit FDA seriousness criterion and the authors themselves use the SAE designation via the study's '(S)AE case report form' (Safety assessment), so SeveritySource='author'. NAffected=5 (1+4) reflects the combined arm counts as printed; the per-arm split is preserved in Description. Onset coded 'unknown' rather than inferred, since the text does not state when during the 4-week-to-6-month follow-up period these relapses/hospitalizations occurred relative to the dosing visit.

config_proposal.note: Cohen's d = 0.151 for abstinence duration (psilocybin vs. placebo, 4-week follow-up) is directly reported by the authors and requires no derivation, so it is a clean d-to-Hedges'-g pass-through. Flagging for human awareness: this same d-value is paired with two different p-values in the article (p=0.55 in the Abstract vs. p=0.37 in the Results narrative) - an unresolved internal inconsistency in the source article that does not affect the d-value itself but affects interpretation of its significance.
